$comment: W-40 (S-1) — reviewed exemption register for the unauthenticated side-effect check.
An entry here says: this route exports a side-effecting method, the check can prove no
sender authentication, and a human has looked at it and named what holds instead.
Adding one is a security decision. Name the model and cite the line that enforces it.
The list may only shrink. A stale entry fails the check. The `ratchet` ceiling is
ENFORCED BY THE CHECK, not only by the lock — over it is a violation, under it is stale,
because a ceiling left above a fallen floor hands out that many free exemptions.
ALL THREE CURRENT ENTRIES ARE THE SAME CLASS, and it is worth stating plainly rather than
burying in three reasons: they are PUBLIC INTAKE. There is no sender to authenticate — an
anonymous prospect holds no credential and never will — so S-1's first two legs (signature,
hashed token) do not apply and the invariant's own third leg, 'an explicit, reviewed
exemption', is the correct disposition. What SHOULD bound them is abuse control, which is
`S-2` / `W-35` ('abuse control becomes a declared property', needs `AD-14`) and is NOT BUILT:
none of the three has a rate limit, a captcha, or any other volume control. Each entry
records the specific unbounded side effect so W-35 inherits a sized list rather than a class
name. These are exemptions from 'authenticate the sender', NOT from 'be bounded'.

exemptions.reason: Unauthenticated marketing demo form. POST validates name/organization/email (:22-31) and then POSTs to https://api.resend.com/emails (:45) delivering to the fixed MARKETING_DEMO_INBOX (:4). There is no sender to authenticate. The side effect is OUTBOUND EMAIL, not a database write: the route touches no Supabase client of any kind, which is exactly why W-4's service-client census could never see it — this route is the concrete proof that W-4's subject and S-1's subject are different sets. UNBOUNDED, and specifically: no rate limit, so an anonymous caller can drive arbitrary volume through the org's Resend account to a single inbox; `reply_to` is caller-supplied (:54) and the subject and body embed caller text (:55-62). W-35's work, sized. Also logs the full payload including the submitter's email at :41 — noted for the same lane, not a separate finding.

Unauthenticated vendor application intake. There is no sender to authenticate. What holds instead is the pair W-4 already reviewed and this check re-verifies: the org is pinned to ALLOY_PUBLIC_ORG_ID from the environment and the route 500s without it (:33-37), never taking an org from the caller; and the handler CREATES ONLY — it selects no existing row by a caller-supplied id, so there is no object it can be pointed at. That is the property whose absence froze W-4's book-v2 baseline. UNBOUNDED: no rate limit, so the side effect is unlimited anonymous row creation in the pinned org. W-35's work.

Public inbound gutter-lead intake, marked LEGACY_COMPAT in its own header. There is no sender to authenticate. Creates only — a contact upsert plus an opportunity create — so as with vendor-application there is no caller-supplied selector reaching an existing row. It reaches a service client through `@/lib/supabase` helpers rather than importing a constructor, which is why W-4 carries it under `advisory_transitive_only` rather than as an exception; it is a genuine S-1 subject either way. UNBOUNDED: no rate limit, no captcha. W-35's work, and W-15 separately holds the question of whether this legacy route should exist at all.
